A character who is not attacking blocks attacks, blaster bolts and thrown lightsabers that come from within the character's block arc. The block arc is the area in front of the character where blocks are possible. The arc is wider at a higher defense level. It is also wider against blades than against bolts. A character with no defense level does not block.

A character blocks an attack when the cosine of the angle between the attack and the character's facing is above a limit. The limit is 0.9 at defense level 1, 0.6 at level 2 and 0.3 at level 3. A lower limit means a wider arc.

A character with a lightsaber blocks blaster bolts at a bolt level. The bolt level starts at the character's defense level. The lightsaber's deflection bonus raises or lowers it. The bolt level is 1 lower while the character jumps or moves backward. At bolt level 1 the blade absorbs the bolt. At level 2 the blade deflects the bolt in the direction the character is looking. At level 3 the blade reflects the bolt back at the shooter.

An NPC who deflects blaster bolts in quick succession can be overwhelmed. Every bolt the NPC deflected in the last 2 seconds counts toward the Overwhelmed rule. This applies under both the Jedi Academy rules and the Advanced rules.

For every bolt an NPC deflected in the last 2 seconds, the next bolt has a chance to get past the NPC's lightsaber and hit them. The chance for each deflected bolt is 16% with Jedi Defense, 12% with Advanced Jedi Defense and 8% with Master Jedi Defense. An NPC without the feat has a chance of 20% for each bolt. The first bolt after a pause is always deflected as usual.

A bolt that an NPC deflects strays further from where the NPC sent it. It strays by up to 0.2 on each axis with Jedi Defense, 0.15 with Advanced Jedi Defense and 0.1 with Master Jedi Defense. An NPC without the feat makes it stray by up to 0.25. This applies under both the Jedi Academy rules and the Advanced rules.

When the blocker's defense level equals the level of the throw, the blocker knocks the lightsaber to the ground with a chance of 4 in 10.

Every character can jump. A character with Force Jump, and any character who has Force points, can also make a Force Jump. A character who has Force points but not the feat jumps at rank 1. When the character keeps the jump key pressed while rising, the Force lifts the character toward the height of his or her rank above the takeoff point. The lift is stronger the farther the character still is below that height. Once the character rises above the height of a normal jump, the Force Jump is active. The character then flips in the direction of the movement key pressed. From rank 2, a character who presses no movement key leaps in the direction he or she is already moving. Force points do not regenerate during a Force Jump, and the character spends Force points while rising.

A normal jump rises 0.81 meters above the takeoff point. Force Jump rises 2.4 meters at rank 1, 4.9 meters at rank 2 and 9.8 meters at rank 3.

Force Jump lifts with a strength of 420 / 590 / 840 at ranks 1, 2 and 3. The character rises at a normal jump's speed plus a tenth of this strength. That tenth is multiplied by the fraction of the jump height still left to rise.

An active Force Jump spends Force points every 0.2 seconds at rank 1 and every 0.3 seconds at ranks 2 and 3.

The amount a Force Jump spends depends on how fast the character is rising. The six amounts apply above rising speeds of 6.4 meters per second / 5.1 meters per second / 3.8 meters per second / 2.5 meters per second / 1.3 meters per second / 0 meters per second, from the fastest to the slowest. A falling character spends nothing.

Each time, a Force Jump spends 20 / 16 / 12 / 8 / 6 / 4% of the character's maximum Force points, from the fastest rise to the slowest. The amount is divided by the character's Force Jump rank.

In KOTOR 1, a character's Force points regenerate 1 point at a time. An empty pool refills completely in 20 seconds, whatever its size. Force points do not regenerate while the character has a power active. In KOTOR 2, the party regenerates Force points by KOTOR 2's own rule, described at the end of this chapter.

An empty pool of Force points refills in 20 seconds, whatever its size. The points return 1 at a time.

Most powers take effect at once. A toggled power stays active for its duration. The toggled powers are the speed powers, Force Aura, Force Shield, Force Armor, Force Resistance, Force Immunity, Affect Mind, Dominate Mind, Fury and Force Sight. If the Jedi uses a toggled power again at the same rank after 1.5 seconds, the power ends. If the Jedi uses a different rank of it, the new rank replaces the old one. While the Jedi's hand is raised for one power, the Jedi cannot use another power that needs a free hand.

A toggled power must be active for at least 1.5 seconds. After that, using the power again ends it.

After using Affect Mind, a stun or fear power, Valor, Energy Resistance, Slow, Affliction, Plague, Force Suppression, Force Breach or Fury, the Jedi keeps a hand raised for 1 second. During that time the Jedi cannot use another power that needs a free hand, and cannot fire a weapon.

A character whose player presses nothing gets up on its own 4 seconds after the knockdown ends. The character raises its weapon once it stands.
